newsitem.title: SPAIN: Chronology of deteriorating Spain-Cuba relations.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of deteriorating Spain-Cuba relations.

text.p: The following is a chronology of steps taken by conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar since he took office in May and adopted a harder line than his Socialist predecessor against Cuban leader Fidel Castro:
May 5, 1996 - Conservative Popular Party (PP) leader Aznar sworn in, ending 13 years of Socialist rule; diplomats expect Cuba to be treated with less sympathy under his government.

May 25 - U.S. Vice President Al Gore visits Spain and Aznar soft peddles Spain's opposition to the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which punishes foreign firms doing business in Cuba, and declines to endorse the former Socialist government's clear stance against the law.
May 25 - Spain says it will stop non-humanitarian aid to Cuba.
May 28 - Ruling PP defeats Socialist and left-wing parliamentary motion to condemn the Helms-Burton law.
June 21 - Spain lodges formal complaint with Washington over U.S. law punishing foreign firms doing business in Cuba.
June 22 - Spain joins 14 European Union partners in expressing deep concern about effects outside the United States of U.S. laws like Helms-Burton.
July 15 - Spanish communist Julio Anguita, leader of third largest parliamentary group, visits Cuba in solidarity against the United States and urges Aznar to use more placatory tone toward Cuba.
July 16 - Spain applauds U.S. President Bill Clinton for delaying lawsuits linked to Helms-Burton.
August 2 - Spanish government decides to change ambassador in Cuba, arguing previous administration was soft on Havana.
September 10 - U.S. envoy visits Spain to urge tougher position on Cuba and praises the conservative government for its harder stance.
Sept 6 - Aznar, on visit to Mexico, publicly calls for democratic reforms and free elections in Cuba.
Sept 12 - Cuba slams Aznar for seeking reforms.
Oct 24 - Spain sends $200,000 in aid to Cuba for victims of Hurricane Lili which battered island a week earlier.
Nov 7 - Spain links cooperation with Cuba to democratic reforms, release of political prisoners and start of economic liberalisation.
Nov 14 - Spain proposes EU policy placing conditions on future EU eonomic cooperation with Cuba; calls for democratic reforms and faster economic liberalistion.
Nov 23 - Castro defends communism in speech to party, blasts Spain and Aznar in particular for calling on Cuba to adopt multi-party system.
Nov 26 - Cuba retracts acceptance of Spanish ambassador.
